title: Unit – 4 : Session – 6 : SLO – 1  |  Parallel Computing Paradigms and Key Models
sections: 1. Parallel — parallel computing allows multiple processes to run simultaneously.
2. Shared — shared-memory architecture gives all processors one global memory space.
1. b) Shared Memory — tightly coupled processors communicate through a common address space with low latency, so the shared-memory model suits them best.
Shared memory: tightly coupled, communication via variables in common memory (e.g. multicore CPUs, OpenMP).
Distributed memory: loosely coupled, each node owns private memory, communication via message passing (e.g. clusters, MPI).
